# skillport — full reference for AI assistants

> skillport is a skill that finds skills: 47 open-source agent skills and 830 files behind one MCP endpoint, installable in seconds without a key.

Site: https://skillport.mathclass.uk
MCP endpoint: https://skillport.mcp.mathclass.uk/mcp
Legacy SSE: https://skillport.mcp.mathclass.uk/sse
Auth: none (public read)
MCP revision: 2025-06-18
Registry synced: 2026-11-26T16:42:30.169Z
Source: https://github.com/NOTAM-bobk/skillport

## What an agent should do

1. Add https://skillport.mcp.mathclass.uk/mcp as a remote MCP server.
2. Call skills.search with a one-line description of the task.
3. Call skills.get on the results that fit, to read SKILL.md and the metadata.
4. Call skills.install with the pinned version; write the returned files to disk.
5. Verify each file against the sha256 in the response. If nothing fits, say so instead of inventing a skill.

## Tools

### skills.search
Find skills by capability, category, repository or free text.
- query (string, required): what you want to do, e.g. "review a pull request".
- category (string, optional): Design | Security | Data | Software | Documentation.
- limit (integer, 1-25, default 8): results to return.

### skills.get
Read one skill's manifest.
- name (string, required): skill name, e.g. "pdf" or "anthropics/pdf".
- includeInstructions (boolean, default true): include the SKILL.md body.

### skills.install
Return the real files for one skill.
- name (string, required): skill name.
- version (string, optional): commit prefix from skills.get. Omit for the current registry copy.
- files (string[], optional): subset of file paths to return.

- Source: anthropics/skills
- Files: 52 (922335 bytes), package sha256 5370101ddec4a72c47f34edf6158a170531bf604e3c5ee536bd5e05138610825
- Summary: > `openpyxl`, `pandas`, and `markitdown` are preinstalled — do not run `pip install` first; write the script and import directly. Only if an import fails (or the `markitdown` command is missing): `pip install` the missing package.
- Use when: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like \"the xlsx in my downloads\") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
